dimensions.title: Cognitive
milestones: Can solve simple problems like puzzles
Can classify objects by color and shape
Can follow two- to three-step instructions
activities: Play simple board games that involve counting
Engage in story-telling with open-ended questions
Encourage sorting games with toys or household items

dimensions.title: Language
milestones: Has a vocabulary of around 1,000 words
Can form sentences of four or more words
Can sing simple songs or recite nursery rhymes
activities: Read interactive books with questions
Play rhyming games
Encourage conversation during daily activities
watchFor: Struggles to be understood by familiar adults

dimensions.title: Physical
milestones: Can jump forward and backward
Can throw and catch a ball with increasing accuracy
Can balance on one foot for a few seconds
activities: Set up an obstacle course for gross motor skills
Engage in activities like dancing or jumping games
Provide arts and crafts that require cutting, gluing, and coloring
watchFor: Limited fine motor skills like drawing or writing

dimensions.title: Social
milestones: Can take turns and share with others
Shows interest in playing with peers
Can express emotions verbally
activities: Organize playdates or group activities
Role-play different social scenarios
Encourage cooperative games like building together
watchFor: Frequent aggression or tantrums during play

dimensions.title: Emotional
milestones: Can identify and label their own feelings
Shows empathy towards others
Can express likes and dislikes verbally
activities: Use feeling charts to recognize and discuss emotions
Encourage storytelling that involves feelings
Provide scenarios to practice emotion regulation
watchFor: Struggles to cope with change or transitions

dimensions.title: Curiosity
milestones: Asks 'why' and 'how' questions frequently
Shows interest in exploring new environments
Enjoys simple experiments to see outcomes
activities: Plan trips to nature walks or museums
Set up science experiments like planting seeds
Encourage creative exploration through arts and crafts
watchFor: Lack of interest in exploring surroundings

dimensions.title: Learning
milestones: Can focus on tasks for up to 15 minutes
Shows persistence in completing tasks
Begins to understand cause and effect
activities: Play memory games to enhance attention
Engage in building activities like blocks or Lego
Introduce simple chores that require focus
watchFor: Easily distracted or unable to maintain interest
Gives up quickly when faced with problems

dimensions.title: Independence
milestones: Can dress and undress with minimal help
Can express preferences and make simple choices
Can manage basic hygiene tasks with supervision
activities: Encourage self-dressing by providing choices in clothing
Assign simple chores like setting the table
Allow them to choose their snacks or meals
watchFor: Dependence on caregivers for routine tasks
Struggles with making choices or decisions
